label: lm_provider_integration_and_configuration
label_description: Users are trying to connect DSPy to specific LM backends—local models, Hugging Face/vLLM servers, OpenAI-compatible APIs, Bedrock, Vertex, and custom endpoints—and make those clients work end to end. Their friction centers on DSPy's LM client wrappers: which providers and API modes are supported, and how endpoint, auth, and request-generation options such as max_tokens, headers, timeouts, regions, and other kwargs are passed through.
selection_notes: Selected eight that stay tightly inside LM/provider integration and configuration while remaining answerable from `dspy/` and `tests/` alone. I cut 2, 12, 13, and 18 as more adapter/parsing-centric than provider-integration-centric; 7, 9, 17, and 19 as narrower overlaps with stronger selected items; and 4, 11, 14, and 16 as strong alternates that lost on diversity or focus.

finalists.question: I'm pointing `dspy.LM` at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The same base URL works from the OpenAI SDK, but one DSPy setup sends chat messages, another collapses everything into one prompt string, and another expects Responses-style `input` blocks. What actually changes between those request modes, and which auth/header settings still reach the backend?
finalists.answer: `dspy.LM` switches transport entirely by `model_type`. `chat` calls LiteLLM chat completion with `model` plus `messages`. `text` flattens message contents into one prompt, appends `BEGIN RESPONSE:`, rewrites the model to `text-completion-openai/<name>`, and resolves `api_key`/`api_base` from kwargs or `<provider>_API_KEY` and `<provider>_API_BASE`. `responses` rewrites chat-style messages into Responses `input` blocks and then calls LiteLLM Responses. Across these paths, extra caller kwargs continue downstream, and DSPy merges `User-Agent: DSPy/<version>` into outgoing headers.
finalists.note: Core OpenAI-compatible endpoint behavior; rewritten to avoid naming the attachment-point attribute in the question.

finalists.question: My usual OpenAI-style setup uses `temperature=0.2` and a small token budget, but DSPy rejects that before sending any request for some model names. Which model families trigger that guardrail, and what token parameter does DSPy switch to when they do?
finalists.answer: DSPy special-cases OpenAI reasoning families in `LM.__init__`. Names matching `o1`, `o3`, `o4`, `o5` with optional `-mini`/`-nano`/`-pro` and optional date suffixes, plus `gpt-5*` except `gpt-5-chat`, must use `temperature=1.0` or `None` and `max_tokens >= 16000` or `None`. For those models DSPy stores the limit under `max_completion_tokens`; other models keep plain `max_tokens`.
finalists.note: High-value constructor-time config trap with concrete model-family logic.

finalists.question: I saved a predictor that used a custom gateway. After loading it in a fresh process, the secret was gone from the file, the gateway URL no longer applied, but text-mode calls still authenticated from the environment. What LM state does DSPy intentionally strip, and how do trusted files opt back in?
finalists.answer: `api_key` is never serialized by `LM.dump_state()`. On load, DSPy strips `api_base`, `base_url`, and `model_list` unless you opt in with `allow_unsafe_lm_state=True`. In text mode, DSPy then resolves `api_key` and `api_base` again from kwargs or the environment, so an environment key can still authenticate even when a serialized endpoint override was ignored.
finalists.note: Good persistence-safety question that stays inside provider configuration behavior.

finalists.question: A bare model name like `gpt-4o-mini` works for ordinary inference, but provider-managed operations later act as if no provider was configured. Why does DSPy treat that LM as OpenAI-like for some checks but not when choosing the provider object?
finalists.answer: DSPy separates provider naming for LiteLLM capability checks from provider-object inference. If the model string has no slash, `_provider_name` defaults to `openai`, so support checks and some environment lookups behave OpenAI-like. But `LM.infer_provider()` only auto-selects `OpenAIProvider` for model strings starting with `openai/` or `ft:`; otherwise the LM gets the base `Provider`, whose `launch()` is a no-op and whose `finetunable` flag is false.
finalists.note: Subtle but repo-grounded distinction between capability inference and provider inference.

finalists.question: I want DSPy to start a local model server for me instead of talking to an existing endpoint. What does the local launch flow normalize from the model name, how does it boot the server, and why is nothing launched unless I opt into the right provider?
finalists.answer: Local launching is provider-driven, not inferred from the model string. You must construct the LM with a local provider; otherwise `launch()` just hits the base provider's no-op. In `LocalProvider.launch`, DSPy strips leading `openai/`, `local:`, and `huggingface/`, picks a free port, starts `python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path ... --port ... --host 0.0.0.0`, waits for `/v1/models`, then writes `api_base=http://localhost:<port>/v1` and `api_key='local'` back onto the LM. The command is built as a list, so spaces and shell-looking text stay literal.
finalists.note: Covers the local-model launch path rather than a pre-hosted endpoint.

finalists.question: I'm using DSPy's Databricks fine-tuning path. Which configuration is mandatory, what Unity Catalog path shape gets validated for uploaded training data, and what comes back if I skip deployment versus letting DSPy deploy?
finalists.answer: Databricks fine-tuning is explicit-provider only; it is not auto-inferred. `DatabricksProvider.finetune` accepts a `TrainDataFormat` enum or the strings `chat` and `completion`, but `train_kwargs` must include both `train_data_path` and `register_to`. The upload target must match `/Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume>/...`. If `skip_deploy=True`, the provider returns `None`; otherwise it deploys the registered model and returns `databricks/<endpoint_name>`, where dots in `register_to` are replaced with underscores.
finalists.note: Strong Databricks-specific integration/config question with concrete path validation.

finalists.question: I want fine-tuning an OpenAI model to hand back another usable LM, not just a remote job id. Which model names select the OpenAI provider automatically, what training formats are accepted, and what provider-side IDs and cleanup state does DSPy track?
finalists.answer: OpenAI fine-tuning is auto-selected only for model strings starting with `openai/` or `ft:`. The provider accepts only chat and completion training data. `OpenAIProvider.finetune` saves JSONL locally, uploads it, stores the upload id on `job.provider_file_id`, starts remote training and stores the remote job id on `job.provider_job_id`, waits for completion, and returns the provider's fine-tuned model name. `LM._run_finetune_job` then turns that string into a copied `dspy.LM`, so `job.result()` is another LM instance. `TrainingJobOpenAI.cancel()` also cancels the provider job and deletes the uploaded file if it still exists.
finalists.note: End-to-end OpenAI provider lifecycle, not just a one-symbol lookup.

finalists.question: I rely on custom headers for auth and tracing. Where does DSPy add its own identifier header, which request paths preserve my headers, and do sync and async streaming behave the same?
finalists.answer: DSPy adds `User-Agent: DSPy/<version>` in `_add_dspy_identifier_to_headers`. Non-streaming chat, text, and responses calls all preserve caller headers through that merge. Sync chat streaming also preserves them because `litellm_completion` forwards headers into `_get_stream_completion_fn`. Async chat streaming is not symmetric: `alitellm_completion` removes `headers` from the request but does not pass them into `_get_stream_completion_fn`, so the downstream streaming `litellm.acompletion` call sees no custom headers.
finalists.note: Excellent pass-through/config question with a real sync-vs-async behavioral mismatch.
